Obama won the 2008 election with 365 electoral votes to McCain's 173, and took office during the worst quarter of the financial crisis: GDP fell at an annualized 8.5% in Q4 2008.

His first major legislation was the $787 billion stimulus, passed in February 2009 with three Republican votes in the Senate. The Affordable Care Act came a year later, after a drafting process that ran through five congressional committees and cost Democrats the House in the 2010 midterms.

What I find hard to summarize is the gap between how he campaigned and how he governed. The 2008 campaign ran on ending a war and closing Guantanamo. Guantanamo was still open when he left. The drone program expanded under him, and the legal memos justifying it stayed classified for years.

He left office with a 59% approval rating. That number is probably the least interesting thing about the presidency.
